lessons.title: Getting ready to empty a bin
lessons.html:
Getting ready to empty a bin

To deplete a bin means to empty it. Grain runs out of the bottom of the bin through an outlet slide onto a conveyor, then goes to a truck, rail truck, another bin, or the dryer. Bins are emptied to dispatch grain, to move grain that is getting warm, or so the bin can be cleaned and inspected.

Before you start

  1. Get the instruction from your supervisor or the control room: which bin, how much grain, and where it must go.
  2. Check the route: the right conveyors, elevator and spouts must be set. Grain sent the wrong way can mix with other grain.
  3. Check that the place it is going to has space: the truck is in position, or the receiving bin is not full.
  4. Check that the conveyor under the bin is clean and the guards are in place.
  5. Put on your PPE: safety boots, dust mask, ear protection and gloves.

How grain flows out of a bin

Grain usually flows out from the middle first. A funnel forms in the centre of the grain, and grain from the top slides down into it. Grain can also stick to the walls and form a bridge or crust, with an empty space underneath. A crust can break suddenly.

This is why nobody may be inside a bin or on the grain while it is being emptied. A person on the grain is pulled into the funnel in seconds and buried.

Example

Themba is told to empty bin 3 into the truck at the loading spout. He checks with the control room that the route is set, confirms the truck is in place, and checks that nobody is on the bin roof or inside the bin before he opens the slide.

lessons.title: Emptying the bin safely
lessons.html:
Emptying the bin safely

Steps

  1. Start the receiving equipment first: the last conveyor or elevator in the route, then work back to the conveyor under the bin. This stops grain piling up and blocking.
  2. Open the centre outlet slide first, slowly. Use the centre outlet until the funnel is finished, then the side outlets as your site procedure says. Opening side outlets first can put uneven pressure on the bin wall and damage it.
  3. Watch the flow. Do not let the conveyor overload.
  4. Keep in contact with the control room and the loading point by radio.
  5. When the amount needed is out, close the slide, then let the conveyors run empty before stopping them.
  6. Record the bin number, date, time and amount.

If the grain stops flowing

  • The grain may be bridging or caked.
  • Close the slide and tell your supervisor.
  • Do not climb into the bin. Do not poke from above while standing on the grain.
  • Only trained people with a permit, harness, lifeline and standby person may enter a bin, and only after all outlets are locked out.

Never

  • Never put hands into a running conveyor or slide.
  • Never remove guards.
  • Never smoke near the bins. Dust can explode.
  • Never leave the slide open and walk away.

Last of the grain

When the bin is almost empty, some grain stays on the floor. Your site may use a sweep auger to move it. The sweep auger is very dangerous. Only trained workers use it, and it must be locked out before anyone goes in to clean.

Key points

  • Get clear instructions: which bin, how much, and where to.
  • Check the route and that the receiving point has space.
  • Start the equipment from the end of the route back to the bin.
  • Open the centre outlet first.
  • Nobody inside or on the grain while a bin is emptied.
  • If flow stops, close the slide and report; do not climb in.
